text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- 'America's double criteria': Vjesnik's chief editor Nenad Ivankovic says in an editorial that the Croatian presidential election won negative evaluation by international observers for practices common in other democratic states -- the United States and Germany.
- Wheat from the Croatian Danubian area (Eastern Slavonia) could end up in Serbia say members of the Vukovar-Srijem county's chamber of commerce and ask the Economy Ministry to prevent it.
- The Croatian pension law could see its first reading in parliament in September. Minister of Labour and Social Care Jozo Skara said the retirement age should be increased from 60 to 65 years.

- Some 25,000 Croats will return to their homes in Eastern Slavonia by September, says Minister for Reconstruction and Development Jure Radic. UNTAES has become a hindrance in the return of Croatian refugees to Eastern Slavonia, that is the joint conclusion of the members of the parliament, the refugee association, governtment's office for refugees and others from a meeting in Zagreb on Wednesday.

- The Zagreb branch of the HSLS, whose candidate Vlado Gotovac came third in Sunday's presidential election, decided to enter a coalition with the ruling HDZ and share power in the capital despite Gotovac recommending against such cooperation.
- U.S. Ambassador to Croatia Peter Galbraith said Serb refugees returning to Croatia should have equal rights as Croats returning to Eastern Slavonia.

- A rich tourist summer about to start. It remains to be seen whether the tourist season will yield 25 or 30 percent more overnights than last year, but the first wave of tourists, both foreign and domestic, is expected next weekend.
- The Croatian parliament discussed loss-making Croatian Railways and how to make the firm profitable.
- Croatian team returned from Puerto Rico, where Croatian dogs won six world champion titles.
- German formula for Croatian pensioners, parliament discusses the pensions bill.
- Islands of Mljet and Lastovo in the southern Adriatic will be supplied by water from machines, designed to desalinate salt water, as part of a pilot project run by national utility Croatian Waters.
- "We saw Gospa (Virgin Mary)", say children from Gradina near Virovitica who claim the Virgin Mary appeared to them at the local soccer ground last Friday. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
